item.title: The Enterprise AI Push For Decision Models
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: The AI race has largely revolved around frontier labs and models that can write, code, analyse documents and reason through…
item.content:encoded:
The AI race has largely revolved around frontier labs and models that can write, code, analyse documents and reason through prompts. But as companies move from chatbots to AI agents, another part of the stack is gaining attention: models that make a specific decision and return an answer that another system can act on.

Decision models gained momentum with the arrival of Jev, the first public model from TypeSafe AI, founded by Diogo Almeida, who helped develop research behind ChatGPT at OpenAI. Released in September, Jev focuses on decision-oriented outputs, including scores and yes-or-no probabilities, rather than conventional text generation.

Other companies have since explored similar capabilities, though their products differ in architecture and intended use. 

Cloudflare has introduced Clef and Clef-flash, while Microsoft has released Decision-1, a model based on Alibaba’s Qwen family that has been post-trained for decision tasks. AWS has introduced Strands Decider 2B for agent workflows, and OpenAI has launched a Decisions API. Perplexity has also explored decision-oriented APIs.

Under this approach, an agent handling a customer complaint, for instance, may need to decide whether to escalate it, route it to a particular team or resolve it automatically. It does not necessarily need a long, generated response to make that decision. The same applies to systems classifying transactions, checking whether an action should proceed or routing requests across software tools.

These decisions can be handled by general-purpose large language models (LLMs), but using them for every step can add latency, cost and complexity. Decision models are designed to handle narrower tasks, returning a label, score, probability or confidence level instead of a paragraph of text.

The idea is to give software a more direct way to make a bounded judgement without requiring a general-purpose model to generate a full response at every stage. In agentic systems, where multiple tools and models work together, this could make routine decisions easier to integrate into a workflow.

They are not necessarily replacements for LLMs. Rather, they can become specialised components within larger AI systems, handling defined decisions while general-purpose models take on tasks that require broader reasoning or language generation.

Enterprises Seek Reliability

For enterprises, the opportunity extends beyond reducing token consumption and cost savings. Companies need AI systems that can work with internal data, understand domain-specific context and make decisions that can be reviewed and governed.

General purpose models are probabilistic by design. Their responses can vary, even when prompts appear similar. That flexibility is useful for open-ended tasks, but enterprise workflows in sectors such as manufacturing, energy, finance and aerospace often require defined outputs, traceability and tighter controls.

Articul8 AI, an enterprise AI company spun out of Intel in 2024, is building a platform around what it calls a “correctness stack”. 

According to Ananthanarayanan S, the company’s managing director for India, enterprises need more than access to a capable model. They need a system that connects their data and domain knowledge with models that can deliver outputs suited to specific workflows.

The platform is designed to work across cloud environments, on-premises deployments and air-gapped systems. Its data perception layer brings information from different enterprise sources into a unified view, helping AI systems work with the context and relationships within an organisation’s data.

Articul8 has developed around 28 domain models spanning areas such as energy, finance, aerospace and manufacturing. Its platform can select models depending on the task and combine specialised models with customers’ preferred frontier or reasoning models. The company says its approach can reduce token usage by more than 50% in relevant workflows, although the savings will depend on the application and deployment.

In October, Articul8 announced Bivia, a multimodal decision model designed to process inputs such as text, images, video frames, tables and charts, and return structured decisions. Ananthanarayanan said the differentiation lies less in any single model than in the platform’s ability to connect models and solve difficult customer problems.

He cited an engineering company with around 10,000 documents that were ingested in roughly 10 hours before an application was made available for use. Articul8 has also said the American Society of Mechanical Engineers selected it for work related to standards. These examples point to the company’s focus on applying AI within existing enterprise workflows rather than selling a standalone model alone.

PurpleTalk is approaching the opportunity through Sthānika, its applied AI research lab, and the Sieve family of decision models. Sieve-31Bv3 is designed to be called by AI agents as one component in a larger system. It returns a defined answer with a confidence score, allowing the agent to decide what to do next.

The company claimed at the time of launch that Sieve-31Bv3 ranked first on the full Jev Decision Index, a collection of 43 private and public benchmarks hosted on Hugging Face. The company reported a score of 71.1 on the full index and 71.7 on the public test, where it ranked third. 

Sieve builds on earlier compact, confidence-aware decision models used within PurpleTalk products Ello and Mina. The company sees potential applications in voice, customer experience and robotics, where routine decisions need to be made quickly and predictably.

“Sieve-31B shows that a focused model fine-tuned in India can perform among the best in the world at this work. The private tests matter most to us. They come from domains outside the public suite, and Sieve generalised better than most of the field. It learned the task, not the test,” said Sridhar Muppidi, cofounder of PurpleTalk.

Bharat Lingam, CEO of PurpleTalk, believes decision models will open up a new category of agentic systems: more reliable, more controllable, and fast enough for voice, customer experience and robotics. “We are publishing everything needed to reproduce our results, and we invite the research community to test it, challenge it and build on it,” Lingam added.

The approaches illustrate two sides of the enterprise opportunity. Articul8 is building a broader platform around enterprise data, models and governance, while PurpleTalk’s Sthānika is a specialised model that agents can call for particular decisions. In both cases, the commercial test will be whether these systems improve real workflows, not simply whether their models perform well on benchmarks.

A Decision Model For Every Workflow

The decision model opportunity is not limited to enterprise platforms in India. Smaller AI startups and researchers are also exploring models that can be adapted, deployed locally and used by developers building their own applications.

Kerala-based ConvAI Innovations has developed Laya, an open-weight decision model intended to run locally on devices such as laptops and mobile phones and be adapted by developers. Founder Nandakishore Mukkunnoth said the initial focus was on building small, fast models that did not always require cloud access. Interest in a general-purpose, open-source decision model grew after Jev’s release.

The startup has discussed plans for Laya Max, with image and audio capabilities, alongside APIs, software development kits and a commercial enterprise offering. It has also suggested that Laya could deliver substantial cost savings compared with Jev. These claims will need to be tested against comparable workloads, as performance and cost depend on the task, model configuration and deployment.

Laya’s significance lies in the possibility of giving developers an adaptable model that can run closer to where decisions need to be made. Local execution could be useful where latency, connectivity, data control or inference costs matter. But open weights alone will not establish a durable advantage. The model will still need to perform reliably on real tasks and be straightforward to integrate into applications.

For investors, the opportunity may be less about backing another general-purpose model and more about identifying where decision-making can become a product in its own right. “Decision models are one of the most important shifts in AI this year. What can’t be copied is a company’s own record of decisions and outcomes. For startups, the real test is how fast the model improves on a specific, high-volume workflow,” said Shubham Gupta, founding general partner at Together Fund.

That points to a potential advantage for startups that can pair models with proprietary data, feedback from actual outcomes and a clearly defined customer problem. A model may be accessible to competitors, but the data and workflow knowledge used to improve its decisions can be harder to replicate.

In the Indian context, this creates several possible entry points: developing specialised models, building infrastructure that routes tasks to the right model, and creating applications around high-volume enterprise workflows. The challenge is to demonstrate measurable improvements in accuracy, cost or speed, rather than compete on benchmark scores alone.

As the global industry moves towards more specialised AI systems, the question is whether Indian builders can turn their models into products that enterprises repeatedly use. The next advantage may not belong to the model that can do the most things, but to the system that can make a particular decision reliably, cheaply and at scale.

item.title: Sachin Tendulkar Backs Hitwicket Parent Metasports
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Former cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has backed Metasports Interactive, the gaming startup behind mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket. The investment terms…
item.content:encoded:
Former cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has backed Metasports Interactive, the gaming startup behind mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket. The investment terms such as size and valuation were not disclosed. 

Tendulkar will continue to feature in Hitwicket’s in-game experiences, content and brand activations. He is the second cricketing icon to have backed the startup in recent times, after Harsha Bhogle’s undisclosed investment in the startup in 2024. 

Overall, the Bengaluru-based startup has raised over $23 Mn cumulatively over the past six years during which it has been operational. Its largest funding round came back in April, when it nabbed $20 Mn from London-based growth financing company Metica to fuel marketing and user acquisition. As part of the deal, Metica is also advising the startup in monetising their gaming app via advertising and in-app purchases. 

Founded by Kashyap Reddy and Keerti Singh, Hitwicket is a strategy-based online multiplayer cricket game for smartphones and tablets. Available on both Play Store and Apple Store, it allows users to play the role of an owner, coach, and captain of a cricket team.

“Hitwicket has built a distinct proposition in cricket gaming by making strategic decision-making central to the experience, and Sachin Tendulkar recognised this unique difference. Interacting with Sachin Tendulkar is helping us understand how elite cricketers think on the field and further improve the game engagement,” said Metasports’ cofounder and CEO Kashyap Reddy. 

The startup says it has a global player base of 20 Mn users across 120 countries, who spend 51 minutes per day on the platform on average. It is looking to scale to over 100 Mn downloads over the next three years. 

In terms of financial performance, it claims its topline grew 100% over the past six months, with more than 97% of its revenue coming from in-app purchases. 

It is pertinent to note that Hitwicket’s partnership with Tendulkar comes as Bengaluru-based rival LightFury Games is gearing up to launch its own mobile cricket game, eCricket, in a closed beta stage. 

LightFury had raised $11 Mn in pre-Series A funding earlier this year and has tied up with marquee cricketers like Rohit Sharma, MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and others to licence their images for its product. 

As of 2025, India had around 511 Mn gamers, while the country’s gaming revenue rose 14.8% YoY to cross the $1 Bn mark – making it one of the fastest-growing markets in the world for gaming, according to Niko Partners. As digital adoption increases, audiences are also increasingly turning their attention beyond just battle royale and casual games to a wider range of genres.

item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain

item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based D2C jewellery brand GIVA has raised ₹975 Cr (about $103 Mn) in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, with participation from existing investors Epiq Capital and Edelweiss Discovery Fund, as it looks to accelerate its offline expansion, strengthen manufacturing capabilities, and widen its product portfolio.

The transaction comprised a mix of primary and secondary capital, alongside an ESOP buyback, GIVA cofounder and CEO Ishendra Agarwal told Inc42.

Early investors India Quotient and Sixth Sense Ventures will partially exit through the transaction while retaining stakes, Agarwal said. Multiples will also secure a board seat.

GIVA’s seventh ESOP buyback, worth approximately ₹20-25 Cr, will benefit around 50-60 employees.

The latest valuation was not disclosed. Agarwal said it was higher than the approximately ₹4,500-4,600 Cr (about $422 Mn to $474 Mn) valuation of its previous publicly announced funding round.

GIVA reported revenue of ₹865 Cr in FY26 as against ₹505 Cr in FY25, according to Agarwal. Its negative EBITDA margin narrowed to single digits from double digits over the same period.

Agarwal attributed the improvement to its maturing store network. Stores operating for more than a year are profitable, he said, with rising same-store sales helping absorb rent and employee costs. GIVA expects to become profitable on a profit after tax (PAT) basis in FY28.

GIVA To Add 160 Stores, Invest In Manufacturing

GIVA operates around 425 stores across India and plans to add 160 outlets in FY27, with a greater focus on Tier II and III markets.

About 70% of its stores are in metros, with the remainder in smaller cities. It plans to deepen its presence in Lucknow, Dehradun, Kanpur, and Surat, while entering markets such as Agra.

Offline retail contributes approximately 45% of revenue, with its D2C channel accounting for 55%. Agarwal expects offline’s share to reach 75-80% over the next three years.

GIVA will also invest in manufacturing capabilities in Jaipur and Mumbai. It outsources bulk manufacturing but handles plating and finishing entirely in-house, along with customised and made-to-order products.

Greater control over plating and finishing would improve product quality and consistency, Agarwal said.

The startup also plans to expand inventory across silver, gold, and lab-grown diamond jewellery, particularly in the ₹10,000-40,000 price range.

Silver Remains Revenue Mainstay

Founded in 2019 as an online-first silver jewellery brand, GIVA has since expanded into gold and lab-grown diamonds.

Silver contributes around 60% of revenue, while gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery together account for 40%, Agarwal said.

Its average selling price (ASP) is around ₹3,500 for silver jewellery and ₹15,000–18,000 for lab-grown diamond jewellery. Blended average order value stands at approximately ₹5,000, with offline orders typically worth nearly twice as much as online purchases.

Within gold jewellery, 9-carat and 14-carat products are gaining traction. Introduced around four months ago, 9-carat gold jewellery now accounts for approximately 25% of its combined gold and lab-grown diamond business.

GIVA is also expanding its men’s portfolio, which contributes around 20% of its silver jewellery business.

Its recently launched demi-fine jewellery brand Ixia remains at an early stage. Agarwal said its revenue was doubling MoM, albeit on a small base.

Building Towards IPO Readiness

The addition of fine gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery has helped GIVA generate more revenue from existing customers. Agarwal said customer lifetime value has doubled among customers moving from silver to lab-grown diamond jewellery.

GIVA aims to become IPO-ready within two to three years, although an actual listing is at least three years away, he added.

The latest investment follows its ₹530 Cr Series C round in June 2025, led by Creaegis. Before the current transaction, GIVA had raised about $164 Mn from investors including PremjiInvest, Northern Arc, and Alteria Capital.

The transaction comes amid investor interest in India’s organised jewellery market, particularly lab-grown diamonds. According to Redseer, India’s lab-grown diamond market was valued at $300–350 Mn in 2024 and is projected to grow at a 15% CAGR over the following decade.

In July, Bengaluru-based Aukera raised ₹90 Cr in debt funding led by Alteria Capital to expand its stores and omnichannel infrastructure. Jewelbox and True Diamond also raised $3.2 Mn and $3 Mn, respectively, in rounds led by V3 Ventures and India Quotient.

item.title: Mobavenue Q2 Profit Rises 54% YoY To ₹11.3 Cr, Revenue Up 41%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Adtech company Mobavenue, formerly known as Lucent Industries, reported a 54.4% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹11.3 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
Adtech company Mobavenue, formerly known as Lucent Industries, reported a 54.4% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹11.3 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹7.3 Cr in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose 41.2% YoY to ₹76.7 Cr. 

Sequentially, the top line increased 5.3% from ₹72.8 Cr, while net profit declined about 3% from ₹11.7 Cr.

Total income, including an other income of ₹1 Cr, stood at ₹77.7 Cr during the quarter, up 42% YoY. Total expenses increased 40.1% YoY to ₹62.2 Cr from ₹44.4 Cr. Supply and data costs, the largest expense component, rose 34.6% to ₹44.9 Cr, while employee benefit expenses increased 63.1% to ₹9.9 Cr.

Profit before tax grew 49.6% to ₹15.5 Cr from ₹10.3 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Tax expense for the quarter increased to ₹4.2 Cr from ₹3 Cr a year ago. 

Along with the financials, the company declared an interim dividend of ₹0.10 per equity share for FY27. It has fixed November 13 as the record date for determining the eligibility of shareholders entitled to receive the interim dividend on equity shares.

The promoters of the company – Prachi, Kunal Kothari, and Tejas Rathod – have voluntarily decided to waive their respective entitlements to receive the interim dividend declared by the company in respect of their respective shareholdings

item.title: Apple Logs Record India Revenue, Mac And Services Hit New Highs
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Apple reported an all-time revenue record in India in Q4 FY26, with its iPhone business setting a September quarter revenue…
item.content:encoded:
Apple reported an all-time revenue record in India in Q4 FY26, with its iPhone business setting a September quarter revenue record and Mac and services revenue reaching new highs.

The company also recorded a September quarter high for iPhone upgraders in India, CEO John Ternus said during its earnings call.

Globally, Apple’s revenue rose 12% YoY to $114.5 Bn in the quarter ended September 26, while consolidated net profit increased 11.8% to $30.7 Bn.


“We also set September quarter revenue records in both developed and emerging markets, in addition to an all-time record in India,” Ternus said.

Apple’s global iPhone revenue rose 17% YoY to $57.6 Bn. Alongside India, the company recorded September quarter highs for iPhone upgraders globally, in the US, and in mainland China.

Citing a recent Worldpanel survey, CFO Kevan Parekh said iPhone was among the top-selling smartphone models in India, the US, urban China, the UK, Germany, Australia, and Japan.

Mac revenue increased 24% YoY to $10.8 Bn globally. The business recorded double-digit growth across developed and emerging markets, with all-time revenue highs in India and Southeast Asia.

“We saw double-digit growth in both developed and emerging markets, with all-time records in markets like India and Southeast Asia,” Parekh said.

Apple also recorded a September quarter high for customers buying a Mac for the first time.

Its services business posted record global revenue of $31.6 Bn, up 10% YoY, with all-time highs across most markets it tracks, including India and Latin America.

Apple Pay’s India Entry


Apple expanded its services offering in India with the launch of Apple Pay on September 30, with Axis Bank as its first banking partner.

The service supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, allowing users to pay through their iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch in apps, online, and at contactless-enabled stores. Mac support is expected to follow, while RuPay cards are not supported at launch.

For in-store payments, users authenticate transactions with Face ID, Touch ID, or their device passcode before holding their iPhone or Apple Watch near a contactless reader.

Apple said actual card numbers are neither stored on devices or its servers nor shared with merchants. It also said it does not retain transaction information that can be linked to users.

The company has partnered with payment infrastructure providers, including Juspay, Cashfree, and PayU, to offer Apple Pay across their merchant networks. Apple said the service is accepted by millions of merchants in India at launch, including Blinkit, Zomato, Croma, ixigo, Tata 1mg, and Chaayos, with more merchants and apps to follow.

“India is home to a dynamic and digitally savvy population that continues to embrace a cashless future while expecting the highest standards of security and privacy, and we’re so excited to bring Apple Pay to users in India today,” Jennifer Bailey, vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, said at the launch.

Apple Pay is available in more than 90 countries and regions and works with over 11,000 bank and network partners globally.

Overall, Apple’s products business generated quarterly revenue of $82.9 Bn, up 12% YoY. However, iPad revenue declined 10% to $6.2 Bn, while wearables, home, and accessories revenue fell 8% to $8.3 Bn.

For FY26, revenue increased 15% to $478.8 Bn. Apple expects December quarter revenue to grow 7-10% YoY, taking quarterly revenue to a new high.

item.title: India Becomes ChatGPT’s Largest Market Globally, User Base Doubles Since January
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: India has become ChatGPT’s largest market globally by weekly active users, with its local user base doubling since January 2026,…
item.content:encoded:
India has become ChatGPT’s largest market globally by weekly active users, with its local user base doubling since January 2026, OpenAI India MD Prabhjeet Singh said.

Speaking to ET, Singh attributed the growth to Indian users increasingly integrating ChatGPT into their everyday workflows and finding more uses for the chatbot.

The milestone follows OpenAI cofounder and CEO Sam Altman’s description of India during his visit last year as the company’s fastest-growing market and second-largest globally by users. In February 2026, OpenAI said India had more than 100 Mn weekly ChatGPT users.

To reach more users beyond major cities, OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT’s Indian-language capabilities and focusing on Android-first product development.

While the company expects paid subscriptions to grow as users find more value in its products, Singh said its immediate priority is expanding AI’s impact. OpenAI is also expected to make announcements concerning UPI and payments in the coming weeks.

Expanding India Footprint

OpenAI announced its first India office in Delhi NCR and began local hiring in August 2025. At the India AI Impact Summit in February, it unveiled plans for Mumbai and Bengaluru offices and launched OpenAI for India to expand access, infrastructure, and enterprise adoption.

Its partnership with TCS’ HyperVault data centre business starts with 100 megawatts (MW) of capacity, potentially scaling to 1 gigawatt (GW). Singh said OpenAI would consider more capacity as infrastructure comes online.

The capacity will address enterprise data residency and security requirements, while privacy and returns on investment remain key adoption considerations. OpenAI models are also available through AWS’ Amazon Bedrock for local inference, keeping request processing within India.

Enterprises Move Beyond Pilots

Singh said enterprises, global capability centres (GCCs), and startups are moving beyond pilots to production deployments, citing JioHotstar and Cars24.

India is also among Codex’s largest and fastest-growing markets, with significant developer use emerging from tier-II cities, he added.

OpenAI is engaging with government agencies, banks, and financial institutions to strengthen cybersecurity and protect critical infrastructure against AI agent misuse. Singh also backed clear AI regulation to build confidence among consumers, enterprises, and developers.

OpenAI is also expanding advertising on ChatGPT in India. Singh said ads would help support free and lower-priced access alongside paid subscriptions.

He added that advertisers would not have access to users’ personal information and that advertisements would not influence ChatGPT’s responses.

The company has partnered with Razorpay to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT. Under the partnership, Razorpay’s growth marketing platform Engage helps brands prepare product catalogues, launch and manage campaigns, and measure performance.

Early participating brands include Tanishq, Fastrack, Traya, Tata Neu, Rivaah by Tanishq, Shaadi.com, Axis Max Life, Palmonas, and Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS).

item.content:encoded:
Peer-to-peer (P2P) lending startup LenDenClub’s parent Vartis Platforms has launched UdhaarSaathi, a digital loan marketplace for small businesses, expanding its lending service provider (LSP) portfolio.

Speaking to Inc42, Vartis founder Bhavin Patel said the platform caters to kirana stores, pharmacies, street vendors, and other small retailers, facilitating collateral-free business loans ranging from ₹15,000 to ₹2.5 Lakh.

With an average loan ticket size of around ₹1 Lakh, Vartis aims to facilitate ₹1,000 Cr in disbursements through UdhaarSaathi by the end of FY27.

The launch comes amid Vartis’ internal preparations for a potential IPO, including strengthening governance across its platforms. Patel said that the company is targeting readiness over the next 12-18 months rather than a listing within that period.

“There is no timeline as yet. The next 12 to 18 months is what we are targeting to prepare ourselves,” Patel said. 

The IPO could comprise an offer for sale (OFS), with Vartis currently seeing no need to raise primary capital. However, it may consider a fresh issue to fund a business opportunity or expansion, he added.

Bringing Credit To Retailers

UdhaarSaathi uses merchants’ banking and business transaction data, shared with their consent, to support credit assessment by its lending partners.

It operates as an LSP and loan marketplace, facilitating credit through multiple NBFCs. Vartis does not take credit risk on loans facilitated through the platform. 

The platform’s first version went live in February, followed by the final version a couple of months ago. West India currently accounts for its largest customer share, followed by the South, East, and North, Patel said. The company expects to share a detailed regional breakdown by December.

UdhaarSaathi is Vartis’ second LSP platform after InstaMoney, which launched in 2017 and primarily serves individuals seeking small-ticket emergency loans. UdhaarSaathi extends this business to merchants seeking working capital. 

Vartis earns fees when repayments are processed through either platform, Patel said.

Founded in 2015 by Patel and Dipesh Karki, Vartis also operates lending technology platform Vartis One.

On the financial front, Vartis’ net profit rose 183% to ₹96.2 Cr in FY26 from ₹34 Cr in FY25. This marked its second consecutive profitable fiscal following a net loss of ₹10.6 Cr in FY24 after the RBI’s crackdown on the P2P lending sector. 

Operating revenue grew 43% to ₹338 Cr from ₹236.4 Cr in FY25. Including interest and other income, total revenue stood at ₹366.6 Cr in FY26.

item.title: The Second Life Of Festive Gift Boxes
item.dc:creator: Meha Agarwal
item.description: Some gifts can be more than just gifts; they can be keepsakes. At least that’s what brands are hoping for…
item.content:encoded:
Some gifts can be more than just gifts; they can be keepsakes. At least that’s what brands are hoping for this Diwali. 

Along with the familiar ritual of exchanging sweets, dry fruits and gifts, D2C brands are hoping that customers sign a covenant of sorts while completing their last-minute festive shopping. Because, once the goodies are gone, most boxes often end up in storerooms or dustbins. 

But D2C players are giving the humble gift box a second job. 

Think handcrafted wooden mini trunks that double up as jewellery organisers or beautifully illustrated tins that find a place on kitchen shelves, or even intricately designed boxes that become decorative pieces in their own right.

When it comes to the festive season, packaging is no longer just about protecting or presenting a product. It is designed to be treasured, reused and memorable. 

Gifting platform IGP has designed a bag that doubles as a rangoli stencil. Meanwhile, Jaipur-based artisanal confectionery Bliss & Bite has taken a more luxurious route, packaging its chocolates in hand-painted Pichwai wooden chests that can later find a second life as jewellery boxes or keepsake organisers.

New-age brands Phool, Nihira Mithai, Nutty Gritties, Petite Pie Shop, The Urban Dori and Parna Varna are among those experimenting with festive gift boxes, reusable tins, keepsake containers and multipurpose hampers designed to have a life beyond the celebrations.

The goal is simple. Get consumers to think about the brand and recall it the rest of the year. In the right home, the packaging becomes a marketing asset. And if the gifting experience proves memorable enough, perhaps they’ll return for another purchase. 

But here’s the business reality: Behind these creative experiments are design costs, minimum order quantities, production timelines and the risk of being left with hundreds of festive boxes once the celebrations end.

So, as D2C brands try to make festive packaging sustainable, more memorable and commercially valuable, one question deserves a closer look: Can a gift box that refuses to become waste also become an investment that pays for itself?

Beyond Brand Recall

For D2C brands, the real test of festive packaging begins after the celebrations end. Beyond making a lasting impression, the focus is on acquiring new customers, encouraging repeat purchases and sustaining the festive sales momentum long after the season is over.

RENÉE Cosmetics’ festive campaigns have consistently delivered an uptick in sales during Q3 of the financial year (October to December), which typically includes Diwali, cofounder and CEO Ashutosh Valani told Inc42. 

The startup claimed that for three consecutive years, sales in the following quarter (January to March) have matched or exceeded Q3 levels. It did not share specific data about each quarter, so the sales numbers could not be independently verified. 

Plus, RENÉE cannot attribute these improvements exclusively to its festive season packaging. If you consider the whole campaign, it includes costs for packaging, storytelling, the product itself and marketing activities. 

So what can brands do to measure their campaign success and performance? For IGP, rather than assigning a packaging-specific sales figure, it is about examining customer reactions, reviews and social sharing. The customer success team also collects feedback that shapes the next year’s campaign design.

Tarun Joshi, founder and CEO of IGP, puts it, “We judge a festive packaging campaign by whether it leaves customers delighted and makes the experience memorable. Customer delight is harder to count, so we make the packaging useful and DIY-friendly, and look at how customers react and share it.”

But once again, we must stress none of these measures conclusively isolates packaging’s contribution from festive demand, product quality or the broader marketing efforts. In other words, brands can measure what happens after these festive unboxing, but not how much of it happened because of the box. 

So, how much should brands spend in terms of both efforts and money on packaging when its returns are so difficult to quantify?

Untangling The Economics 

The cost of festive packaging can be relatively easy for an established brand to absorb. For an early stage startup, however, the same exercise can put considerable pressure on margins, pricing and operations.

Valani told us the additional cost has a marginal 1-2% impact on RENÉE’s gross margins, with growing scale and declining customer acquisition costs making it easier to absorb. 

IGP, meanwhile, treats creative packaging as advertising expenditure, sometimes building entire campaigns around it.

But the equation changes for early stage startups such as Farm Didi. The startup begins preparing its festive hampers six to eight months before Diwali, coordinating reusable packaging, handcrafted products and production across rural women’s groups. This makes festive gifting a resource-intensive exercise, leaving little room for aggressive discounts.

“That is why it is very important for us to target the right set of customers. We are not looking to target those customers who are looking for heavy discounts,” added Farm Didi cofounder Manjari Sharma.

For smaller brands, minimum order quantities (MOQs) add another layer of risk. Lifestyle brand Includ cofounder Ashwin Rastogi pointed out that customised packaging often requires brands to commit to minimum production volumes across multiple sizes, making the investment difficult to justify if demand falls short. Unlike established players, early stage brands may not have the sales volumes to absorb these costs.

So, while larger brands have more flexibility to absorb or justify packaging expenditure, newer or smaller players must find ways to make every order commercially viable. But even favourable unit economics cannot solve one problem – what happens when brands invest in festive packaging and the expected orders never arrive?

Unlike a digital campaign that can be paused, unsold gift boxes can remain in inventory long after the festivities end. This brings us to a more fundamental question: Should every brand be investing in festive packaging in the first place?

Taking The Gamble

In conversation with industry leaders and startups, it became evident that not every brand needs a Diwali hamper to outshine its competitors and create strong brand recall. Brands need to remember that they need to sell the hampers too to recover their investment.

Arjun Vaidya, founder of Dr Vaidya’s and now an investor at V3 Ventures, believes that brands need to recognise if they have a qualified sales pipeline in the months and weeks before Diwali.

“We are not a Diwali brand, and if you are in the same place, don’t waste time, effort and energy to buy these boxes and do this packaging because it’s a big cost. Having inventory on hand can quickly become a problem,” Vaidya explained.

The problem is that festive packaging has an expiry date. A Diwali-themed box may be difficult to sell once the festival is over, leaving brands with inventory they cannot easily repurpose.

Yet, avoiding festive gifting altogether isn’t necessarily the answer. Food, fashion and certain premium products naturally lend themselves to gifting. Everyday essentials, however, may struggle to attract buyers simply because they come in a festive box. Channel partnerships may drive sales for such brands.

Even for brands in the right categories, execution matters. Festive hampers must offer something genuinely different and, importantly, be priced for the intended customer. A beautifully designed box alone cannot justify an unrealistic price tag.

Rather than competing during peak festive sales, when marketplace traffic costs are high, Includ founder Rastogi suggested occasions such as Halloween and Christmas, where competition is relatively lower and the opportunity to stand out is higher.

Brands can assess whether the additional demand generated will be large enough to justify the upfront investment, inventory risk and higher cost of competing during the season.

Although brands are increasingly pitching reusable packaging as a greener alternative to conventional gift boxes, the real question is how many of these premium wooden boxes, elaborate hampers and reusable containers actually find a second purpose in customers’ homes? 

The challenge is that brands have limited visibility into what happens after unboxing. This creates a distinction between packaging that delivers marketing value and packaging that delivers measurable environmental benefits.

A box worth photographing or keeping may strengthen brand recall, but that alone does not make it a right choice if the product itself is not up to par.

THE STARTUP SPOTLIGHT | HOW HYEGLO BEAUTY IS BRINGING SKINCARE SCIENCE INTO EVERYDAY MAKEUP 

  • Hyeglo Beauty is building a skin-first colour cosmetics brand by combining makeup pigments with clinically tested ingredients and functional skincare activities. It claims that its formulations are designed to deliver makeup coverage while supporting skin hydration and overall skin health.
  • Its product range includes tinted moisturisers, lip and cheek balms, and lip oil stains, with prices ranging from ₹799 to ₹1,350 on its website. 
  • The startup follows a D2C-led model, selling through its own website. It is looking to build its presence in India’s colour cosmetics market, competing with established and emerging makeup brands. 

THE DEEP DIVE

ECOMMERCE BUZZ

Numour’s Fundraise: The D2C skincare startup founded by Divya Jain in 2025, is reportedly in talks to raise $3.1 Mn from Sharrp Ventures. e startup combines skincare formulations with beauty devices and sells products across its website, ecommerce marketplaces and quick commerce platforms. 

AI Kitchen Startup’s Fundraise: Smart kitchen appliance startup upliance.ai is in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn–$4 Mn in a Series A round. The startup uses generative AI to automate cooking processes and plans to use the proposed funding for R&D, product improvements and international expansion.

Troovy’s ₹100 Cr Bet: The healthy snacking startup has raised ₹100 Cr in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures. The startup plans to expand manufacturing and offline distribution while entering new categories, including namkeen, biscuits and cookies.

Bijnis’ B2B Quick Commerce Pivot: Bijnis has rebranded as Zorit and raised ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital. The Delhi-based startup has shifted from a manufacturer-retailer marketplace to an inventory-led B2B quick-commerce model, delivering products to neighbourhood retailers from local dark stores.

item.title: Exclusive: Nuuk To Raise ₹100 Cr From Wipro Consumer Care Ventures, RPSG At ₹500 Cr Valuation
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: D2C home appliances brand Nuuk is raising around ₹100 Cr (about $10.5 Mn) in a funding round led by Wipro…
item.content:encoded:
D2C home appliances brand Nuuk is raising around ₹100 Cr (about $10.5 Mn) in a funding round led by Wipro Consumer Care Ventures and RPSG Capital Ventures at a valuation of about ₹500 Cr (about $53 Mn), sources told Inc42.

The proposed fundraise would be larger than Nuuk’s $6.6 Mn Series A round, which it closed in August 2025 following a $2 Mn extension from existing investors Vertex Ventures SEA and Good Capital.

The final round size and valuation could change depending on how the discussions progress, the sources added. 

Questions sent to Nuuk, Wipro Consumer Care Ventures, and RPSG Capital Ventures did not elicit a response till the time of publication.

Founded in 2023 by Gazal Kalra, cofounder of logistics unicorn Rivigo, and Shalabh Gupta, former chief growth officer at Noise, Nuuk sells design-focused home and kitchen appliances.

Its portfolio spans cordless vacuum cleaners, fans, heaters, and garment care products, alongside kitchen appliances such as air fryers, juicers, and mixer grinders.

The startup sells through its own website, ecommerce marketplaces Amazon and Flipkart, and quick commerce platform Blinkit. It has also entered offline retail, including a store in Delhi NCR.

While announcing its Series A extension, Kalra told Inc42 that the capital would support portfolio expansion, product innovation, and a wider business footprint. Part of the funding was also earmarked for expanding its domestic supply chain.

In March 2025, Gupta told Inc42 that Nuuk manufactured around 20% of its products in India and aimed to increase this share to over 50% by the end of FY26. Kalra said the company designed its appliances in-house and worked with third-party manufacturers.

On the financial front, Nuuk’s operating revenue rose to ₹16 Cr in FY25 from ₹31.8 Lakh in FY24, according to its MCA filings. FY25 was its first full year of operations. Its net loss widened to ₹39 Lakh from ₹7 Lakh, while expenses increased to ₹16.4 Cr from ₹38.8 Lakh.

The brand competes with established appliance makers such as Philips and Bajaj, alongside newer players including Atomberg and Lifelong.

Investors Back Appliance Startups

Nuuk’s proposed fundraise follows recent investments in home and kitchen appliance startups, with capital going towards product development, manufacturing, and distribution.

In October, smart kitchen brand Beyond Appliances raised ₹110 Cr in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors. The startup said it plans to use the funding to establish a manufacturing facility and expand its portfolio into ovens.

Earlier, home appliance brand Nester raised ₹19 Cr in a pre-Series A round in February 2026. Its portfolio includes steam air fryer ovens, toasters, and juicers.

Meanwhile, Inc42 reported last week that upliance.ai was in advanced talks to raise $3-4 Mn in a Series A round. The proposed funding would support R&D, improvements to its interface, and international expansion, with existing backer Khosla Ventures looking to invest further.

The investments point to investor interest in brands developing differentiated appliances – from connected chimneys to automated cooking devices – and building the manufacturing and distribution networks needed to scale.

item.content:encoded:
MobiKwik Turns It Around

MobiKwik minted its highest-ever quarterly profit in Q2 FY27. The record performance came on the back of its financial services business delivering healthy revenue growth, while a tight leash on expenses helped the fintech company improve margins. 

Here’s a quick glance at MobiKwik’s Q2 FY27 numbers: 

  • Net profit of ₹11.8 Cr compared to a net loss of ₹28.6 Cr in Q2 FY26
  • Operating revenue rose 9.4% YoY to ₹295.7 Cr 
  • Total expenses declined a marginal 1.8% YoY to ₹290.9 Cr
  • EBITDA profit stood at ₹22.7 Cr against an EBITDA loss of ₹6.4 Cr in the year ago quarter

Lending Grabs The Spotlight: MobiKwik’s financial services business picked up in a big way in Q2 as the company disbursed a lot more loans and partnered with more lending partners during the quarter. At the same time, better loan book quality helped reduce expenses and improved the vertical’s gross profit. 

Payments’ Mixed Show: Although MobiKwik’s payments business processed much higher GMV in Q2 on a YoY basis, revenue barely grew. This is because the transaction mix skewed heavily towards payments that generate lower revenue. While this helped bring down payments gateway costs, the business’ take rate took a major hit.

Unlocking Operating Leverage: The quarter also saw both of MobiKwik’s core businesses expand their contribution margins, which helped offset the increased fixed expenses. Going forward, the company sees growing AI adoption in lending, engineering, customer experience, and risk management to further improve operating leverage and efficiency.

As the listed fintech company looks for a way to translate higher transactions into more revenue, here is a closer look at MobiKwik’s Q2 FY27 results…

From The Editor’s Desk

Pixxel CEO Clears Air On US Foray

  • Cofounder and CEO Awais Ahmed has clarified that the spacetech startup remains Indian-owned, managed and controlled amid criticism over the launch of its US subsidiary, Pixxel Federal.
  • The clarification comes after fellow spacetech startup GalaxEye highlighted its decision to operate through a single Indian entity, indirectly questioning the practice of setting up multiple entities across jurisdictions.
  • Pixxel launched Pixxel Federal to pursue US government contracts across civilian, defence and intelligence agencies. The startup, which has raised around $195 Mn to date, also plans to go public in India in the coming years.

Fireside Ventures’ Cofounder Quits

  • Cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the venture capital giant after nearly a decade-long stint. The investment firm is yet to announce his successor.
  • Singh now plans to “explore” the agentic commerce space and its implications for the future of consumption.
  • In his decade-long tenure, Singh grew the firm into a major consumer-focused VC firm. It has so far backed more than 65 Indian startups and manages assets of around $650 Mn across four funds.

ESDS’ Q2 Profit Surge

  • The AI company reported a 40.7% YoY jump in consolidated net profit to ₹31.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue surged 48% to ₹138.3 Cr.
  • The company’s EBITDA rose 18.3% YoY to ₹57.8 Cr, even as its EBITDA margin narrowed to 41.8% from 52% a year ago. Total expenses increased 63.7% to ₹103.5 Cr.
  • ESDS secured a $1.25 Bn AI cloud infrastructure deal with an Australia-based neocloud provider, with revenue expected from Q3 FY27. The company is also expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities through GPU clusters and its SWARAJ Cloud platform.

Record October For UPI

  • UPI transaction volume rose 5.8% MoM to a record 25.47 Bn in October, while transaction value increased 7.4% to ₹31.53 Lakh Cr, according to NPCI data.
  • October marked the first time UPI transactions crossed 25 Bn in volume and ₹30 Lakh Cr in value, driven partly by festive-season spending. On a YoY basis, transaction volume grew 23%, while value rose 16%.
  • The record growth comes ahead of the proposed rollout of MDR charges on select UPI payments above ₹2,000. NPCI deferred the implementation until after Diwali, with a revised date yet to be announced.

Pronto Founder’s Physical AI Bet

  • Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s physical AI venture Provision Labs has acquired Mumbai-based hardware startup Basilisk for an undisclosed sum. As part of the deal, Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani will join Provision and lead its hardware efforts.
  • Founded in 2023, Basilisk is focused on perception technologies, which help machines interpret their surroundings. The startup claims to have developed a 3D hand-tracking model and built the first version of a tactile glove to capture touch-related data. 
  • This comes as Sardana recently launched Provision Labs to collect data for training and testing physical AI systems. The startup has also ramped up hiring of engineering and research teams across San Francisco, Toronto, and Bengaluru.

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Indrajaal Is Building India’s Shield Against Hostile Drones

As drones become cheaper and autonomous, defending borders and critical infrastructure against them is becoming more and more harder. To fix this gap, Indrajaal is building an integrated AI platform to detect, identify and neutralise hostile drones in real time.

Eyes In The Skies: Founded in 2024, Indrajaal is building a counter-drone ecosystem to secure India’s airspace. Its SkyOS platform brings together radars, radio-frequency sensors, cameras and AI to identify aerial threats and execute responses. It also offers a mobile counter-drone vehicle (Ranger), a spoofer called Repulsor and SkyCop, an interceptor drone.

Hunting Hostile Drones: Indrajaal claims that its systems are deployed at installations belonging to the Indian Army, Indian Navy and agencies under the Ministry of Home Affairs. On the back of this, the startup closed FY26 with a revenue of ₹100 Cr and is targeting a top line of ₹300 Cr in FY27. 

The Road Ahead: Indrajaal now plans to raise ₹420 Cr in a Series A round in the near term to expand manufacturing, R&D and its footprint in the Middle East and Europe. The startup also wants to build an autonomous airspace ecosystem for aerial transport. item.title: PowerUp Money Raises $10 Mn To Expand Wealth Management Services
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures,…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC. 

The startup plans to use the capital to expand its AI-led wealth management offerings, scale its managed advisory business and develop personalised financial planning solutions for Indian investors.

“We started by making high-quality investment advice accessible to every Indian. Today, AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally and at a fraction of traditional costs. A significant portion of this investment will go towards building an AI-powered wealth manager that brings personalised financial planning and ongoing portfolio guidance to every Indian,” PowerUp’s founder and CEO Prateek Jindal said. 

Jindal, who has also cofounded fintech major Uni Cards, launched PowerUp in 2025 to help customers manage their mutual fund portfolios. It claims to have over 15 Lakh customers, who track mutual fund portfolios worth over ₹2.5 Lakh Cr on its platform. Its mutual fund advisory subscription, PowerUp Elite, has over 1 Lakh paid members. 

Beyond mutual funds, the startup is now looking to combine investment advice, managed wealth services and digital advisory, becoming a full-stack financial planning platform in essence. 

The first step towards its new avatar has now come with the launch of its end-to-end digital wealth advisory offering, Elite Prime. The service includes an AI wealth coach and personal assistant, considers users’ financial goals, risk profiles and existing portfolios while helping them manage their portfolios and supporting their investment decisions. 

It is also seeking to scale up its managed wealth advisory offering, Infinite, to a broader customer base. 

Aimed at investors seeking more hands-on financial support, Infinite combines personalised financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation, goal-based strategies, ongoing portfolio management and dedicated adviser support.

PowerUp claims that Infinite has scaled to nearly ₹500 Cr in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch.

item.title: Clinics On Cloud Bags ₹120 Cr To Take Its Health ATMs Global
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Health tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised ₹120 Cr (around $12.5 Mn) in its Series A funding round from…
item.content:encoded:
Health tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised ₹120 Cr (around $12.5 Mn) in its Series A funding round from Model42, the medtech-focused investment arm of UAE-based backer Enlightened Minds Investments.

The Pune-based startup raised the fresh funds at a valuation of ₹600 Cr ($63.3 Mn)

In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to bolster its AI-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and accelerate the growth of its micro-clinic ecosystem. 

A chunk of the funding will also be used to strengthen its manufacturing capacity, scale strategic partnerships with healthcare providers and expand global footprint. 

“For eight years, we have built Clinics On Cloud with a simple belief that quality healthcare should never depend on someone’s pincode. This investment gives us the opportunity to take that vision global…,” said Clinics On Cloud cofounder and CEO Abhay Agarwal.

Founded in 2018 by Abhay and Manashrri Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud manufactures and deploys AI-powered “health ATMs”, portable box clinics and mobile medical units that deliver point-of-care preventive health checkups and telemedicine consultations. These solutions enable hospitals and government agencies to set up temporary micro-clinics.

It claims to have so far seen more than 3,500 deployments across 200 cities in India and seven other countries. Having screened more than 1.2 Cr patients so far, the startup claims to cater to the Indian Army, Navy and the Border Security Force (BSF).

The Pune-based startup now plans to position UAE as its global expansion hub, with an eye on exploring new markets across Africa, the US and Southeast Asia.

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in the healthtech sector, which is seeing renewed funding activity on the back of AI adoption. In September this year, smart ring maker Ultrahuman raised $70 Mn to fuel its integrated healthtech playbook.

In July, another AI-powered healthtech startup CARPL.ai also bagged $10 Mn in its Series A funding round led by International Finance Corporation (IFC). In the same month, actor Kunal Kapoor banded together with crowdfunding platform Ketto’s cofounders Varun Sheth and Zaheer Adenwala to launch healthtech startup MetaGO. 

At the heart of all this is the homegrown healthtech market, which is projected to become a $37 Bn opportunity by 2030.

item.title: Fireside Ventures’ Cofounder & Partner Vinay Singh To Step Down
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a nearly decade-long stint. In…
item.content:encoded:
Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a nearly decade-long stint.

In a statement, the venture capital (VC) firm said that Singh would “transition out of the firm”. The consumer-focused fund has so far not named his successor.

On his future course of action, Singh said that he now plans to explore the “frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption”.

“… As AI reshapes commerce faster than most of us expected, I want to spend more time exploring the frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption. I am excited for this next chapter, and deeply grateful to the Fireside family, and to every founder and LP (limited partner) who trusted us on this journey,” said Singh.

An alumnus of IIM Bangalore, Singh counts nearly two decades of experience under his belt. He previously worked at companies like Hindustan Unilever and Bankbazaar. He earlier also cofounded car servicing platform Stepni, which was later acquired by Quikr.

He eventually cofounded Fireside Ventures alongside Kanwaljit Singh, Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu in 2017. Over the past decade, the VC firm has emerged as one of India’s biggest consumer-focused venture funds and counts more than 65 startups in its portfolio. 

It currently claims to oversee more than $650 Mn in assets under management across four funds. The VC firm last closed its fourth fund at about $253 Mn in December last year. The investment firm currently claims to be helmed by a team of 12 principals and vice presidents.

The development comes as a host of seasoned fund managers depart major VC firms to set up their own funds. Earlier this year, Ashish Agrawal, Ishaan Mittal and Tejeshwi Sharma quit Peak XV Partners to establish their own fund, Mettle Capital. 

Private equity (PE) firm L Catterton’s partner and co-head of India investments, Anjana Sasidharan, also stepped down from the company in March this year to set up Asthrum Capital. Another former Peak XV trio, comprising Shailesh Lakhani, Harshjit Sethi and Mayank Porwal, has launched Ambition Capital and is looking to raise $250 Mn for the maiden fund.

item.title: ideaForge Returns To Profitability In Q2, Reports Net Profit Of ₹6.5 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Dronetech major ideaForge posted a net profit of ₹6.5 Cr in the September quarter (Q2) of FY27. The company reported…
item.content:encoded:
Dronetech major ideaForge posted a net profit of ₹6.5 Cr in the September quarter (Q2) of FY27. The company reported a profit in the fiscal year FY26 before dipping back into the red in Q1, reporting a loss of ₹2.6 Cr. It had reported a loss of ₹19.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

ideaForge’s operating revenue grew 124% YoY to ₹91.3 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹40.8 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, it rose by about 33% from ₹68.6 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Defence business, which includes UAV platforms and related solutions for military and security applications, accounted for 72% of Q2 FY27 revenue, while civil applications, catering to commercial, industrial and government applications outside defence, contributed 28%.

Including other income of ₹6.3 Cr, the company’s total income for the period stood at ₹97.6 Cr. 

Meanwhile, total expenses surged 41.9% YoY to ₹90.1 Cr. At ₹48.1 Cr, the cost of materials consumed to manufacture the drones constituted more than half of the total expenditure for the quarter. 

The company turned EBITDA positive during the quarter, reporting an EBITDA profit of ₹23.2 Cr against an EBITDA loss of ₹8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA margin improved to 25.4% from negative 19.6% in Q2 FY26.

ideaForge said that it entered FY27 with an order book of more than ₹300 Cr, of which 50% was executed in the first half of the fiscal.

“As we enter the second half of FY27, our immediate priority is to sustain the pace of execution while bringing our new platforms closer to commercialisation. The combination of an expanding product portfolio, stronger indigenous technology capabilities and growing procurement opportunities gives us confidence in the road ahead,” ideaForge CEO Ankit Mehta said. 

Besides the financial disclosures for the quarter, the company also said that it has secured an investment of  ₹151 Cr from the Technology Development Board (TDB) via the RDI Fund to develop YETI, its logistics unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The UAV is being developed for applications such as cargo transportation, medical evacuation and personnel deployment, and can carry payloads of up to 200 kg.

Shares of ideaForge ended today’s trading session 1.75% higher at ₹639.70 apiece on the BSE.
